actor.name: Allan Pasco
actor.source: approver message of 2026-10-14: "I approve the revised product direction and contract in PR #13. Close the document-review cycle and proceed with the human approval-record and merge steps already described." The same message approves the design only: it is not a claim that phase-1b automation is implemented or verified, automatic merging stays disabled until the implementation passes its acceptance tests, milestone zero is finished first, and the complete sequential workflow is then demonstrated on the reference application. It followed the direction of 2026-10-14 and three rounds of corrections, and named two closing requirements that are incorporated in the content bound here: an automatic merge must be of content verified and reviewed with main as it then stands, refreshed when main moves, and a failing integration result must leave the originating worker able to make a bounded in-scope repair even when its story is done.

subject: PRD 0.9.2 to 0.10: the approved contract defines done, with tests and recorded reviews as its evidence; gate 2 approves the build contract and gate 3 authorizes execution of the plan, so stories are implemented, reviewed, verified and merged by agents under machine-checked conditions instead of a human approval each; gate 4 becomes acceptance of the product and is never delegated; delegation narrows to bounded decision rights during build; new REQ-26 pre-build gap review and REQ-27 product verification; milestone zero keeps its per-pull-request approval unchanged. The phase-1b reference application is named as the second project, resolving open question 2; and, from the approver’s two closing requirements, an automatic merge must be of content verified and reviewed with main as it then stands, refreshed when main moves, while a failing post-merge verification of main reopens the story that caused it for a bounded repair inside its own scope even when that story is done, with everything unrelated held.
scope: The gate-1 record 0001 as amended by 0002 and 0004 remains valid for every unchanged requirement; this amendment re-approves the ten changed ones and approves REQ-26 and REQ-27, whose before hash is null because they are new.
